source_text: Reform Judaism regards brit milah as a symbolic covenantal rite rather than an absolute requirement, often emphasizing the welcoming ceremony, naming, and parental blessings over the surgical act itself, which may precede via hospital circumcision or be omitted entirely by families citing ethical concerns about infant autonomy and bodily integrity. [6]
